analyst_view.overall: Early view: Braga host Arouca five days after their Monday game at Casa Pia and five days before a Conference League trip to Brann. Arouca are 5th and the league's most controlled side under Vítor Severino, conceding 8 in 11, while Braga have just come out of a winless spell with two straight league wins. The site sees a comfortable Braga home win; Arouca's defence suggests it will be harder than that.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean lower: Arouca have conceded 8 goals in 11 games, and Braga's attack has produced just 13. Arouca's 11 games have averaged under two goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, most for Braga. Arouca like to keep the ball and slow the game down, which may limit Braga's attacking spells, but Braga at home will still have the territory. I stay with the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards. Arouca lead the league for effective playing time, which points to fewer stoppages and fewer fouls. I lean a little lower, although Arouca have had some late red cards, like Rukavina's after the final whistle of a game at Alverca.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.6 shots, 15.0 for Braga. That fits Braga at home against a compact visitor, and I found nothing to change it. Braga's Conference League game in midweek could mean some rotation.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target. Arouca's organised defence keeps attempts away from goal, and Braga have not been clinical. I lean slightly lower.
